title: Illinois Hail Exposure Report
summary: Where roof-damaging hail and owner-occupied homes overlap, 2021 to 2026. All 102 counties scored, and the 484 ZIP codes in the top 15 counties ranked into three targeting tiers.
card: Hail exposure by county and ZIP code, with 72 Tier 1 target ZIPs led by the southwest Chicago suburbs.
sourcesShort: NOAA Storm Events, NOAA SPC, NOAA MRMS radar and the U.S. Census Bureau

layers.label: Targeting Tier
layers.blurb: Tier 1 is the top 15% of ranked ZIP codes by score with a hail index of at least 2.0. Tier 2 is the top 40% with at least 1.0.

layers.legendFoot: Share of homes = share of owner-occupied single-family homes in the areas shown. Detail rows: report and radar days count days with 1 inch+ / 1.75 inch+ hail. ZIP codes outside the top 15 counties are not scored.

sections.title: Top 15 Counties
sections.intro: The top 15 counties hold 74% of the state's {stateHomes:int} owner-occupied single-family homes. Read the hail index and the score together: Peoria and Tazewell rank on homes, not hail.

items.title: The County Cut Is Volume-Weighted
items.text: Peoria (14th) and Tazewell (15th) make the top 15 on housing count, with hail indexes of 0.83 and 0.92. McLean misses at 16th, yet insurer claims clustered in Bloomington in April 2026 and Chenoa in May 2025. Bloomington 61701 ranks 70th of all Illinois ZIP codes and Belvidere 61008 ranks 56th: both are worth adding if the campaign has room.

items.title: July to October 2026 Is Preliminary
items.text: NOAA Storm Events data ends in June 2026. The last three months rest on 42 preliminary Storm Prediction Center reports, and for January 2021 to June 2026 the final Storm Events count was 1.58 times the preliminary one, so recent ground counts will rise. Radar covers those months fully.

items.title: No Public ZIP-Level Claims
items.text: The latest NICB Illinois hail claim figures cover 2017 to 2019, and the Illinois Department of Insurance publishes no county or ZIP hail data. Insurer storm releases confirm the ranking where they overlap but cannot replace claims counts.

methods.title: Hail Index
methods.text: Two measures, each divided by its Illinois average and averaged 50/50. Radar: days with NOAA MRMS maximum estimated hail size (MESH) of 29 mm or more over each area, plus double weight at 38 mm or more. Ground reports: days with a 1-inch-plus report within 5 km, triple weight at 1.75 inches or more. 2021-2022 storms count half, 2023-2024 once and 2025-2026 twice, because roofs are usually replaced within a year or two of a storm.

methods.title: Score and Tiers
methods.text: Score = hail index × owner-occupied single-family homes, times a roof age factor of 1 minus half the share built in 2010 or later. The top 15 counties by score are kept, and every ZIP code whose largest land share sits in one of them is ranked on one list. Tier 1: top 15% by score (rank 73 or better) with a hail index of at least 2.0. Tier 2: top 40% (rank 194 or better) with at least 1.0. Tier 3: the rest.

methods.title: Stability
methods.text: Re-running the ranking with every year weighted equally, 1.75-inch hail weighted 2 times and the index 70% radar keeps the same top three ZIP codes and 60 of the 72 Tier 1 ZIPs. Treat Tier 1 as a safe core and ranks inside Tier 2 as a band.

methods.title: Homes
methods.text: Owner-occupied single-family homes, detached and attached, from the U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey 2020-2024 5-year estimates (tables B25032, B25036, B25037). ZIP codes are 2020 Census ZIP Code Tabulation Areas; PO-box ZIPs are not ranked. Renter-occupied, multi-unit and mobile homes are excluded.

methods.title: Hail Data
methods.text: NOAA Storm Events Database, January 2021 to June 2026, and Storm Prediction Center preliminary reports, July 1 to October 6, 2026: 1,757 reports of 1 inch or more. NOAA MRMS MESH daily maximums, January 2, 2021 to October 7, 2026, 2,105 days with none missing. Damage checks used insurer releases, local news and City of Chicago re-roof permits.
